subject.title: [Bug]: sandbox-browser noVNC clipboard garbles non-Latin-1 characters (CJK, Cyrillic, etc.)

question: Should OpenClaw replace the sandbox-browser x11vnc/Xvfb stack with an Extended Clipboard capable VNC/display server, and what observer security contract must that implementation preserve?
rationale: The bug is source-supported, but the likely repair changes the sandbox-browser VNC/display-server boundary and the earlier candidate PR showed concrete auth and binding pitfalls that require maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a secured VNC replacement
options.body: Replace x11vnc/Xvfb with an Extended Clipboard capable server only if the patch preserves VNC auth, localhost-only raw VNC exposure, tokenized observer URLs, CDP startup behavior, Docker image contracts, and live noVNC paste proof.

options.title: Solve text entry through browser actions
options.body: Keep the noVNC stack unchanged and address non-Latin input through a separate CDP/browser action path, accepting that the noVNC clipboard panel remains Latin-1 limited.

options.title: Document the limitation for now
options.body: Leave x11vnc in place and document the noVNC UTF-8 clipboard limitation until a sandbox-browser owner chooses a secure VNC-stack direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a secured VNC replacement
recommendation.body: Replace x11vnc/Xvfb with an Extended Clipboard capable server only if the patch preserves VNC auth, localhost-only raw VNC exposure, tokenized observer URLs, CDP startup behavior, Docker image contracts, and live noVNC paste proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for sandbox-browser introduction and noVNC auth hardening points to steipete.
